question:
A particle moves $5$ units towards east and then $12$ units towards north.
(i) Find the total distance travelled and the magnitude of its displacement.
(ii) Identify which of these quantities is scalar and which is associated with a vector.
explanation:
Step 1: Total path length
The distance travelled is the sum of the lengths of the two parts of the path.
\(\text{Distance}=5+12=17\text{ units}\)
Step 2: Displacement magnitude
The eastward and northward displacements are perpendicular. Therefore, the magnitude of the resultant displacement is
\(|\vec{d}|=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=\sqrt{25+144}=13\text{ units}\)
Step 3: Classification of quantities
Distance has magnitude only and is therefore a scalar. Displacement has both magnitude and direction and is therefore a vector.
Final Answer
The distance travelled is $17$ units, while the displacement has magnitude $13$ units. Distance is scalar and displacement is vector.

options.A:
(i) Distance $=17$ units and displacement magnitude $=13$ units.
(ii) Distance is a scalar, while displacement is a vector quantity.
options.B:
(i) Distance $=13$ units and displacement magnitude $=17$ units.
(ii) Distance is a vector, while displacement is a scalar quantity.
options.C:
(i) Distance $=17$ units and displacement magnitude $=12$ units.
(ii) Both distance and displacement are scalar quantities.
options.D:
(i) Distance $=13$ units and displacement magnitude $=13$ units.
(ii) Both distance and displacement are vector quantities.
